title: Optimization Assessment
metaDescription: A baseline assessment that measures current security and operational performance against defined Best-in-Class criteria before a roadmap is proposed.
heroDek: GSS does not propose a roadmap before establishing where the organization actually stands. The Optimization Assessment measures current state against defined Best-in-Class criteria, so every recommendation that follows is built against a real gap.
contextHeading: A roadmap without a baseline is a guess with a budget
contextParagraphs: Improvement plans commonly start from a generic maturity model, or from whatever the last audit happened to flag. Neither reflects where a specific organization actually stands relative to the standard it is trying to reach, and both tend to produce roadmaps that are broad instead of prioritized.

The Optimization Assessment establishes that baseline directly: current performance across leadership practices, standards, self-assessment, corrective action, and existing KPI instrumentation, measured against defined Best-in-Class criteria drawn from INPO, WANO, and IAEA principles. The output is a gap analysis, not a scorecard — it identifies which gaps carry the most consequence and which are simplest to close first.
That prioritization is what turns the assessment into a roadmap leadership can actually fund and staff, rather than a list of everything that could theoretically be improved.

methodology.label: Scoping & Criteria Definition
methodology.body: Best-in-Class criteria are defined for the specific organization and mission, not imported unmodified from a generic model.

methodology.label: Document & Program Review
methodology.body: Standards, procedures, self-assessment records, and corrective action history are reviewed against the defined criteria.

methodology.label: Field Observation
methodology.body: Direct observation of leadership walkdowns, working-level behavior, and existing KPI practice against the same criteria.

methodology.label: Structured Interviews
methodology.body: Interviews across leadership and working levels surface gaps that documentation alone won't show.

methodology.label: Gap Analysis & Prioritization
methodology.body: Findings are ranked by consequence and difficulty to close, not simply listed.

methodology.label: Roadmap Development
methodology.body: A phased improvement roadmap with milestones is built directly from the prioritized gap list.

faq.q: How long does an assessment take?
faq.a: Scope drives duration — a single-site assessment is a different engagement than a multi-site program review. GSS scopes duration and cost against the specific organization during an initial consultation rather than quoting a fixed timeline.

faq.q: Does the assessment produce a public report?
faq.a: No. Findings, including anything touching specific vulnerabilities or protective-strategy detail, are delivered directly to leadership and held internally.

faq.q: Can this run alongside a scheduled regulatory audit?
faq.a: It can, though GSS typically recommends running it separately so the organization gets an honest baseline rather than an assessment shaped by preparing for the regulator.

ctaHeading: Know the gap before you fund the roadmap
